metadata.input_source: Product brief (Agent 1 input) for KiroSpec Studio

executive_summary: KiroSpec Studio turns a one-paragraph product idea into a validated market, architecture, cost, compliance and DevSecOps package in minutes. It targets small engineering teams that must justify and plan a build without a dedicated analyst, architect or legal reviewer.
problem_statement: Small product teams spend one to three weeks producing the artifacts a build needs before the first line of code: market sizing, competitive scan, architecture and cost estimate, privacy review and delivery plan. The work is repetitive, requires four different specialties, and is usually skipped or done badly, which is why teams discover an unviable market or an unaffordable infrastructure bill after they have already built.
proposed_solution: A web studio where a person describes an idea once and four AI agents produce, concurrently, a market strategy report, an architecture specification with an AWS cost projection, a privacy and licensing review, and container plus CI/CD scaffolding. Each section is published as soon as its agent answers, so the person reads the market analysis while the rest is still generating, and the whole package can be downloaded as a ZIP ready to commit.

tam.source: Aggregate of software planning, requirements management and architecture tooling spend

sam.source: Teams of 5 to 200 engineers adopting AI-assisted planning tooling

som.source: Reachable share over 3 years through developer-led adoption

trends: AI coding assistants moved from autocomplete to whole-artifact generation, making multi-document output credible
Spec-driven development is regaining traction as teams try to keep AI-generated code aligned with intent
Cloud cost awareness moved earlier in the lifecycle: teams now want a cost estimate before committing to a stack
Privacy and licensing review is shifting left as regulators broaden the scope of data protection rules
market_analysis.why_now: Models are finally reliable enough to emit structured, schema-valid documents rather than prose, and teams already trust AI for code, which removes the adoption barrier for AI-generated planning artifacts.

direct_competitors.name: Notion AI + templates
direct_competitors.strengths: Already adopted by most teams, flexible documents, low friction to start
direct_competitors.weaknesses: No schema validation, no architecture or cost reasoning, output quality depends entirely on the operator's prompt
direct_competitors.pricing: $10 per member per month on top of the workspace plan

direct_competitors.name: Jira Product Discovery
direct_competitors.strengths: Native to the Atlassian workflow, strong prioritization and stakeholder views
direct_competitors.weaknesses: Focused on idea triage, produces no architecture, cost or compliance artifacts
direct_competitors.pricing: Free for creators, about $10 per creator per month at scale

direct_competitors.name: Miro AI
direct_competitors.strengths: Excellent for collaborative diagrams and workshop-style discovery
direct_competitors.weaknesses: Visual-first, no structured handoff to engineering, no validated documents

direct_competitors.name: In-house prompt libraries
direct_competitors.strengths: Free, tailored to the team's own conventions, no procurement needed
direct_competitors.weaknesses: No validation, no repeatable structure, drift as soon as the author leaves the team

indirect_competitors: Generic ChatGPT sessions with hand-written prompts
competitive_landscape.differentiation: Four specialized agents write to declared JSON schemas, so every section is machine-validated before it reaches the screen, and the output is a set of repository-ready files instead of a chat transcript.

personas.name: Luis

personas.name: Marina

personas.goal: Hand engineering a brief that already answers the architecture, cost and compliance questions they always ask

jtbd: When I have a raw product idea, I want a defensible market read, so I can decide whether to build it at all
When I am about to start a build, I want an architecture and a cost estimate, so I do not discover an unaffordable bill in month three
When I collect user data, I want to know which regulations apply, so I do not ship an obvious privacy gap

customer_pains: One to three weeks of planning work before any code exists
Four specialties needed for a single decision
Cost surprises discovered after the architecture is locked in
Privacy and licensing reviews postponed until they become blockers
customer_gains: A complete planning package in minutes instead of weeks
Consistent structure across every project and every team
Repository-ready artifacts rather than prose to transcribe
An explicit cost comparison between MVP and scale scenarios
pain_relievers: Concurrent agents publish each section as soon as it is ready, so the wait is never blocking
Every section is validated against a declared schema before it is shown
The AWS cost projection is itemized per service for two scenarios
The compliance review states the triggering facts and what still needs verification
gain_creators: One-click ZIP with the report and the container, CI and hook scaffolding in their destination paths
Assumption panel that lets the person correct what the system inferred before generating
Task list already ordered by dependency level
Six-tab report that reads like a finished document, not a chat log

risk_assessment.risk: Model output quality varies between runs, so two people with the same idea may get analyses of visibly different depth
risk_assessment.mitigation: Declared JSON schemas with minimum lengths and item counts per section, plus schema validation before rendering, so a shallow answer is rejected rather than displayed

risk_assessment.risk: Market sizing figures are model estimates and can be wrong by an order of magnitude
risk_assessment.mitigation: Label every magnitude as estimated or sourced, show the basis next to the value, and never reformat or round the delivered figure

risk_assessment.risk: Four public generation endpoints invoking a paid model are a cost-abuse vector
risk_assessment.mitigation: Rate limiting per IP or a shared header key before any public deployment, plus per-request size caps and a per-source timeout

risk_assessment.risk: Teams may treat the compliance section as legal advice
risk_assessment.mitigation: Explicit non-advice notice, four-level applicability scale that separates mandatory from verification-required, and a justification naming the jurisdiction and triggering facts

justification.viability: Willingness to pay is plausible against the cost of the manual work, but per-generation model cost sets a floor on pricing
justification.desirability: The pain is universal among small teams and the current workaround is visibly bad
justification.feasibility: The pipeline is four schema-constrained model calls plus a rendering layer, with no novel infrastructure

gtm_signals.positioning: The planning package your build needs, generated and validated in minutes
gtm_signals.pricing_model: Freemium with a per-generation quota, then a flat team tier
distribution_channels: Content on spec-driven development and AI-assisted planning
traction_strategies: Public gallery of generated reports as proof of output quality
Free tier generous enough to complete one real project end to end
Downloadable ZIP that lands directly in the user's repository

recommendations.summary: The pain is real, the workaround is bad, and the technical path is short. Ship the six-tab report with schema validation and incremental publication, then measure whether teams return for a second generation.
assumptions_to_validate: Teams trust an AI-generated cost projection enough to act on it
The assumption confirmation step is enough to make a one-sentence idea produce a useful report
Per-generation model cost stays below the price a small team will pay
suggested_experiments: Run 20 real ideas through the pipeline and have engineers grade each section as usable or not
A/B the assumption panel against direct generation to measure its effect on output usefulness

architecture: Four concurrent generation endpoints, one per agent, no aggregator
Schema validation at every boundary, before rendering and before responding 200
Per-source timeout and independent retry, so one slow agent never blocks the others
implementation: Incremental publication: open the output screen as soon as the first section is available
Client-side ZIP packaging with destination paths preserved
Read-only presentation of every generated artifact, escaped as plain text
